title: Use a parameter
explanation: QuoteService ..> FeePolicy is a dependency from client to supplier. quote receives the caller's FlatFeePolicy object and calls feeCents. The service declares no fields; this method does not retain the policy. Cents are integers, so 1250 means 12.50 units of currency.

title: Swap behavior through the interface
explanation: The same quote method accepts FreeAbovePolicy. At or above 1000 cents the fee is zero; below it the fee is 50. The interface signature stays unchanged while totals change. A stable API still has a behavioral contract.

title: Construct a local collaborator
explanation: quoteWithDefault constructs new FlatFeePolicy(50) into a local variable and calls quote. No field is needed for this concrete source dependency: compiling this method still requires FlatFeePolicy and its constructor. The local variable's scope does not specify the object's lifetime.

title: Store an injected collaborator
explanation: new QuoteSession(flat) receives an existing policy through its constructor and stores it. QuoteSession --policy--> FeePolicy describes this retained association. Dependency and association describe different aspects of the design: the session also depends on the policy API. Constructor injection does not decide ownership.

title: Rebind the caller variable
explanation: After flat = threshold, the next parameter-based quote uses FreeAbovePolicy. The session still holds the original FlatFeePolicy reference, as does saved. Java passed a reference value to the constructor; it did not link the session field to the caller's variable.

title: Reject a broken contract
explanation: The lambda subtotal -> -1 is a Java-valid FeePolicy implementation, but breaks its documented nonnegative-result contract. QuoteService rejects it after calling it. The saved policy remains callable. These observations do not promise rollback of arbitrary collaborator side effects or garbage-collection timing.
